title: Earthquake Response
description: Learn the vital steps of 'Drop, Cover, and Hold On' during an earthquake to protect yourself from falling debris.

scenes.text: You are sitting at your desk in school. Suddenly, the ground begins to shake violently. Books start falling off the shelves.
An earthquake is happening! QUICK, what do you do first?

choices.feedbackText: Running outside during an earthquake is extremely dangerous. Things can fall on you while you run.
Exactly! DROP to your hands and knees, COVER your head and neck (preferably under a sturdy desk), and HOLD ON.

scenes.text: You need to find cover. Tap the safest place in the classroom to take cover.

choices.feedbackText: Yes! A sturdy desk will protect you from falling debris.
You should seek cover underneath a sturdy piece of furniture like a desk, not near windows or tall bookshelves.

scenes.text: The shaking stops after a minute. Your teacher instructs everyone to evacuate to the school ground safely. You followed the disaster protocols and stayed safe!
